Yes, Genesis 1 describes a covenant creation
No, Genesis 1 is the physical creation
How do you relate AD 70 to the final hope?
Some put the weight on AD 70 and keep the future hope simple: resurrection and judgment. Others say the new creation began in Christ's resurrection and will be completed in a renewed world.
AD 70 ended the old order; the future holds resurrection and judgment
The new creation has begun and will be completed physically
Do texts like Ecclesiastes 1:4 and Psalms 104:5, which say the earth abides for ever, shape how you read 'pass away'?
If the earth lasts for ever, 'pass away' may mean 'pass into a new form', like the garment changed in Psalms 102:26.
Yes, the earth will be changed, not abolished
No, those texts speak of this age only
In 2 Peter 3:10, is the earth 'burned up' and gone, or 'found' (laid bare) and purified?
Older Greek manuscripts read 'found' (heurethēsetai). Many read this as exposure for judgment and purging, like the flood (3:6). Others follow the reading 'burned up' and see the old world replaced.
Laid bare and purified, like the world after the flood
Burned up and replaced by a new creation
Physical renewal

The present universe will be purged and renewed at Christ's return, not annihilated. Romans 8:19-22 and Acts 3:21 point to creation set free. Held widely by Reformed and many evangelical teachers today.
The present heavens and earth will be destroyed by fire and God will make a wholly new creation (2 Peter 3:10-12; Revelation 20:11). Common in popular dispensational teaching.
Covenantal with future resurrection
Matthew 24:35 and much of 2 Peter 3 describe the end of the old covenant order in AD 70. A future bodily resurrection and final judgment remain. This is the partial preterist reading.
Full covenant-world fulfilment

All 'heaven and earth' passing texts, the resurrection and Revelation 21 were fulfilled by AD 70. The new heavens and new earth are the new covenant world believers live in now. This is the full preterist reading; Genesis 1 is still the physical creation.
Covenant creation of Genesis 1

Genesis 1 itself describes God forming a covenant people, and the 'first heaven and earth' that passed in AD 70 was that covenant world. A minority view within full preterism, contested by most because of Exodus 20:11.
Already and not yet

The new creation began with Christ's resurrection (2 Corinthians 5:17), passed a key stage when the temple fell in AD 70, and will be completed in a renewed world at his return. Many partial preterists and amillennialists hold this.
In Genesis 37:9-10, who does Jacob say the sun, moon and stars represent?
The nations of Canaan
His own household
The angels
The twelve months
Jacob reads the dream at once as himself, his wife and his sons. It shows heavenly lights can picture a covenant family.
Which Hebrew phrase from Genesis 1:2 does Jeremiah 4:23 use for Judah's ruin?
Tohu wabohu, 'without form, and void'
Ruach elohim, 'the Spirit of God'
Yehi or, 'let there be light'
Toledot, 'generations'
Jeremiah describes the land after Babylon's attack as creation undone, using tohu wabohu.
According to Josephus (Antiquities 3.7.7), the tabernacle's most holy place stood for what?
Heaven, kept for God
The underworld
Josephus says the two outer parts were like land and sea, open to people, while the third was set apart for God like heaven.
Isaiah 13:10 speaks of stars that give no light. Which nation was the oracle about?
Egypt
Edom
Assyria
Isaiah 13:1 names Babylon, and 13:17 names the Medes as the attackers. Babylon fell to them in 539 BC.
Which nation is judged when 'the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll' in Isaiah 34:4?
Moab
Isaiah 34:5-6 names Edom (Bozrah). Edom's land remained, so covenant readers see a nation's end described in cosmic terms.
Which text does the covenantal reading use to show the earth itself 'abideth for ever'?
Ecclesiastes 1:4 says generations come and go but the earth remains. Psalms 104:5 and 78:69 say the same.
In Jeremiah 31:35-36, what are the sun, moon and stars used for?
Signs of coming judgment
A guarantee that Israel's place before God will last
Symbols of the twelve tribes
Calendars for feasts
God says that only if those fixed orders fail could Israel's seed cease. The fixed sky guarantees the new covenant promise.
In Hebrews 12:26-28, what remains after God's final shaking?
The Sinai covenant
The earthly temple
A kingdom which cannot be moved
The law of Moses
Hebrews says what is shaken is removed so that the unshakable kingdom remains, and believers 'are receiving' it now.
How does Paul use the Greek word stoicheia ('elements') in Galatians 4:3, 9?
For atoms and molecules
For stars and planets
For the basic rules of the old order
For the letters of the alphabet
Paul calls them 'weak and beggarly elements' tied to days and months. The covenantal reading applies this sense to 2 Peter 3:10.
In 2 Peter 3:6, what 'perished' in the flood, though the planet remained?
The world that then was
The heavens
The stars
Peter says the world then, overflowed with water, perished. Covenant readers stress that the planet survived and only an order of people was judged.
Which detail in Isaiah 65:20 makes covenant readers say the 'new heavens' are not a world without death?
The wolf and lamb feed together
A child shall die a hundred years old
Jerusalem is a rejoicing
They shall build houses
Isaiah 65:20 still mentions death and sinners. This fits a new covenant order in history better than the final state.
What is the main point on which partial and full preterists differ about heaven and earth?
Whether AD 70 happened
Whether Matthew 24:35 refers to AD 70
Whether a future bodily resurrection and renewed creation remain
Whether Isaiah 65 is about the new covenant
Both apply much of the passing language to AD 70. Partial preterists keep a future resurrection and final judgment; full preterists place them in the first century.
Which seventeenth-century scholar applied 'the passing away of heaven and earth' to the destruction of Jerusalem and the Jewish state?
John Lightfoot
John Darby
Cyrus Scofield
John Lightfoot (1602-1675) wrote that the Jewish state was destroyed as if the whole frame of the world were dissolved. John Owen made a similar case on 2 Peter 3.
Which verse is the strongest objection to reading Genesis 1 as a covenant creation?
Exodus 20:11 grounds the Sabbath in the six days when God made heaven, earth, the sea and all in them. Most covenant readers keep Genesis 1 physical for this reason.
